title: The newspaper article by J. C. Thomas about Gil
summary: Johnston mentions a journalist's article about Gil. Anita reads its opening lines about his 1912 birth and step-father's name.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I have not read anywhere else. And as a matter of fact, Joe Thomas I think his name is, who was at the concert Sunday, said to me ......
Who's Joe Thomas?
Isn't his name........ Bill Thomas, Bill Thomas isn't it? Yes.
It may be J.C.
Oh, that's it. All these Thomases, yes.
I don't know what those initials stand for........
Who has a card. Yes, he has a card on which he describes himself as 'renaissance man for rent'. (LAUGHTER).
Is that what it said on his card?
Yes. (LAUGHTER).
He gave me his card but I didn't read it. He was handing them out to everyone.
But anyway he sent to me the very next day a copy of the article which he had written about you. There's no indication
as to what periodical it appeared in, but nevertheless, I do have the article.
A newspaper, I think it was (serial?).
The New York, The Herald, it was a paper around for a while. I don't know if it still exists. A Sunday, every Sunday or maybe even every other.
I used to read his (column) but I never did ever read (this card inaudible ?).
I thought you might want to read this about geographic (pictures on a ?) luxurious montage. In 1912 he was .........
I think you might read that speak a little bit louder.
Oh, I keep forgetting you're on tape. Oh no, I........
Oh no, go ahead, do that, do that.
Well I thought I would check it with Gil, I mean .........
That's okay, go ahead.
Because he can react to something........

In 1912 the new born son of a doctor in Toronto. A few years later he took the name of his step-father Evans. His childhood was divided between Ontario, British Columbia and the States of Washington and California.
